messages:
maria: noticing a ton of 502s from inference-router in us-east-1 GPU pool. pods can't establish outbound connections to modelcache, errors look like connection reset or ECONNREFUSED. any network folks awake?

maria: adding context: errors started ~15:08 UTC after a scheduled batch job.

david: are these cross-node calls or external egress? i.e., SNAT required?

maria: east-west between pods across nodes. kube-proxy set to iptables. traffic volume spiked after a batch job kicked off ~15:10 UTC.

leo: grabbing conntrack stats from affected node.

leo: ```
root@gpu-node-07:~# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
131068
root@gpu-node-07:~# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
131072
dmesg | tail -n 5
[123456.789012] ip_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
``` 

oncall-bot: ALERT: conntrack table at 99.995% on gpu-node-07 (us-east-1). Automated mitigations disabled.

david: yup that's the symptom. table size default is too low for these GPUs with ephemeral short-lived gRPC connections. can we bump conntrack_max temporarily?

leo: we can. quick safe plan: 1) sysctl bump to 200k on hotspot nodes, 2) reduce probe frequency for modelcache service, 3) add Prom alert for conntrack > 85%/node. will do step 1 on canary node now.

kai: note: clearing conntrack entries will drop active connections; prefer increasing limits & shortening timeouts to reclaim entries faster.

leo: applied on gpu-node-07 (canary):

```bash
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=20
``` 

leo: conntrack count stabilized and 502s declined within 30s. metrics show connections per-second dropped after health-check tweaks.

maria: nice. what's the root cause besides default table size? we should avoid repeated incidents.

david: causes: high churn from frequent HTTP liveness probes (1s interval) + client libraries opening short-lived gRPC connections per request + some pods doing external API calls via NAT. Also saw MTU mismatches: some nodes configured 9000 MTU but overlay VXLAN path is 1450 -> fragmentation + retransmit increases churn.

maria: ugh. RDMA usage could help for bulk intra-node transfers, but not for typical gRPC. options:
- enable kube-proxy ipvs to reduce conntrack workload
- centralize heavy egress through a few NAT gateways with higher conntrack capacity
- update AMI to set higher nf_conntrack_max by default
- reduce health-check aggressiveness and switch to kubelet TCP checks where possible

kai: added: update network MTU documentation and enforce consistent MTU at provisioning to avoid fragmentation.

leo: follow-ups actioned:
1) infra: create AMI patch to set net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000 and TCP timeouts (leo)
2) platform: test kube-proxy ipvs on staging (kai)
3) eng: lower liveness probe frequency for modelcache and switch to tcp probe where supported (maria)
4) ops: add Prom alert and runbook for conntrack saturation and escalate to eng-infra (david)

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-459 conntrack saturation, us-east-1 gpupool. Severity: P2.

maria: thanks team. we'll keep monitoring the canary rollout and post an incident summary + RTC item. please paste follow-up logs in this thread.

leo: posting 15m of conntrack graphs in ops dash; will attach link here once uploaded.

maria: assign PM to track longer-term: avoid SNAT for intra-cluster calls via NodeLocal DNS or direct pod routes where feasible.

david: noted. starting a short RFC for NAT-local routing and ipvs migration.

oncall-bot: NOTE: automated mitigation suggestions saved to runbook: increase-nf_conntrack, tune-timeouts, audit-healthchecks.

maria: closing for now, will reopen if errors spike again.
